subject: Embeddings latency surge after model-catalog sync — Acme production impact
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@acme-analytics.com>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.example>
Date: 2027-02-20T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: embeddings endpoint — sudden p95/p99 spike after catalog sync

Hi Jasmine,

We started seeing a sharp increase in embeddings latency in our production workload right after the model catalog sync at ~08:48 UTC. p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~1.2s and p99 is now over 3.8s. This is causing timeouts in our vectorization pipeline and downstream search jobs are backing up.

Attached are a condensed trace and a p95/p99 snapshot from our clients. We rolled no changes on our side. Can you confirm whether Redwood pushed any model variants or catalog promotions around that time? We need an ETA on mitigation — this is affecting our SLAs.

Attachments: acme_trace_20270220.json (traces, 2.3MB), p95_p99_report_2027-02-20.csv (summary)

Thanks,
Laura Chen
Ops, Acme Analytics

From: jasmine_liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.example>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.example>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.example>
Date: 2027-02-20T09:28:00Z
Subject: Re: embeddings endpoint — sudden p95/p99 spike after catalog sync

Laura —

Thanks for the heads up and for the artifacts. I'm escalating this immediately. Preliminary check: we did run a staged catalog sync at 08:45 UTC that promoted a narrower-precision variant for a set of embeddings models (catalog v2027-02-20.1). That rollout should have been traffic-routed only to canary pools but I will confirm routing.

Monica (CS) and Rishi (SRE on-call) are looped in. Rishi — can you triage traces, confirm whether the degraded tail latency correlates with the new variant, and advise on a mitigation (route-back or rollback)?

Laura — we will keep this thread as the single source of truth. I will also create INC-78945 and post updates.

-Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

From: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.example>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.example>, Laura Chen <laura.chen@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.example>
Date: 2027-02-20T09:40:00Z
Subject: Re: embeddings endpoint — sudden p95/p99 spike after catalog sync

Laura — sorry for the disruption. Quick options while we triage:
- We can pin Acme's production routes to the previous model revision (catalog v2027-02-19.4) — should be fast if you give us permission.
- Alternatively, we can enable a temporary throttling policy (increase timeout/retries) on your client route while the engineering team inspects.

If you prefer pinning, please confirm and I'll route the change through our change window (expect ~7-10 minutes to take effect).

Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.example>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.example>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.example>, laura.chen@acme-analytics.com
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.example>, markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.example>
Date: 2027-02-20T10:03:00Z
Subject: Re: embeddings endpoint — sudden p95/p99 spike after catalog sync

Triage update (10:03 UTC):
- Verified: tail latency increased coincident with traffic shifting to variant "embed-v2-q4" at 08:46:12 UTC.
- Observed behavior: embed-v2-q4 exhibits intermittent KV-cache miss amplification for long-tail batch sizes; sustained CPU spikes on host pool gpu-emb-12 leading to increased token-level latency.
- Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/embeds/acme-prod?from=2027-02-20T08:30:00Z&to=2027-02-20T10:00:00Z

Suggested immediate mitigation: initiate urgent rollback of catalog v2027-02-20.1 for Acme routes and force-route to v2027-02-19.4. This should reduce p95/p99 within one routing-cycle (~5–8 minutes).

Requesting approval to execute rollback now. I will coordinate with Monica to confirm timing with Acme.

-Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
SRE, Redwood Inference (on-call)

From: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.example>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.example>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.example>, jasmine_liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.example>
Cc: tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.example>
Date: 2027-02-20T10:12:00Z
Subject: Re: embeddings endpoint — sudden p95/p99 spike after catalog sync

Thanks for the quick triage — this matches an inverse of our benchmarking signal for the q4 quantized variant on medium-seq workloads. We missed a workload corner-case in the canary selection that underrepresents batch composition.

From product POV: please rollback traffic for Acme asap. Engineering will follow with a hotfix to the kernel selection heuristics and modify the canary criteria to include longer batched sequences.

Also flagging for leadership: this will need an exec note for Acme (impact, mitigation steps, credit proposal). Jasmine / Tessa, can one of you prepare a short customer-facing summary once rollback is confirmed?

-Markus
Markus Klein
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference

From: tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.example>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.example>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.example>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.example>, markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.example>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.example>
Cc: laura.chen@acme-analytics.com
Date: 2027-02-20T16:40:00Z
Subject: Re: embeddings endpoint — sudden p95/p99 spike after catalog sync

Rollback completed and validated at 16:22 UTC — Acme routes now pinned to v2027-02-19.4. Verified p95 back to ~110–140ms and p99 under 420ms on sample traffic.

Laura / Acme: deeply sorry for the disruption — we will issue a service credit for the affected window and share a root-cause and remediation timeline by tomorrow EOD. Monica will follow up on the credit and next steps.

Monica: please draft the customer note and include the metrics we observed pre/post rollback. Jasmine — can you coordinate the exec summary for internal leadership?

Laura Chen <laura.chen@acme-analytics.com> replied: "Thanks for the fast response — rollback helped, appreciate the proactive credit offer. We'll stand by for the RCA."

-Tessa Morgan
VP Sales, Redwood Inference
